title: Empty the Mind
coreMove: Emptying the mind means treating thoughts as visitors, not orders: notice the noise, release what is useless, and return before reaction spends the room you need for choice.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose inbox thoughts start acting like commands
exampleSpecs.stakes: one person lets the thread own the hour while another clears enough room to answer the real request
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: two named people face the same noisy thread and opposite approaches produce opposite outcomes

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who wait for ideal conditions before thinking clearly
exampleSpecs.stakes: the review can stall while the protagonist blames the room or move once he separates outer noise from inner command
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: a peer gives one quotable reframe that changes the protagonist's first move

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who think mental clearing means having no thoughts
exampleSpecs.stakes: a confused learner either quits the exercise or learns what the confusion is teaching
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the learner's mistaken blank-mind standard becomes the material of the lesson

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who let alerts and guesses merge under pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same report either spreads panic or separates facts from mental residue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the same person repeats the same process before and after clearing the mind

exampleSpecs.audience: readers reviewing a messy failure after the fact
exampleSpecs.stakes: understanding depends on finding the small record that shows where noise became command
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: nothing new happens except a reviewer discovers the telling detail in existing files

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose thoughts argue while the work is open
exampleSpecs.stakes: the protagonist can obey the surge or clear enough room to leave the reply for better judgment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the whole scene stays inside one mind and includes wrong turns before the release
